$comment: Where every device photo came from, and under what terms.
This file is the reason the image set can grow past a dozen devices without
becoming a problem. A photo with no recorded origin cannot be checked later, and
at five hundred entries 'we found it somewhere' is not an answer anyone can act on.
Two kinds of entry live here and they carry different obligations:
vendor  - the manufacturer's own product shot. Used the way every companion app
uses them. Not a licence grant; recorded so it can be replaced if asked.
cc-by-sa - Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike. Attribution is mandatory and
has to appear in the About page. Our cropped version is a derivative and
carries the same licence, which is why 'derivative' is spelled out below.
Every image here is 512x512 WebP, background keyed out, subject centred with a 6%
margin. That uniformity matters more than the individual pictures: a list where one
row is a studio render and the next is a snapshot on a desk reads worse than a list
of plain glyphs. A photo that cannot be brought to this standard does not go in -
the class silhouette is the better answer, not a worse one.
Devices absent from this file on purpose: Apple AirPods Pro 2 and JBL Flip 6. Both
appear in the design; neither has a product shot we can stand behind, and both are
devices we only read from. They get their class silhouette, which is what the tail
of the catalogue will look like anyway.

apple-airpods-pro-2.reason: The only freely licensed photo found is a hand-held snapshot on a desk (Commons, CC BY-SA 4.0, by aconcagua). Wrong framing for a 56 px row; Apple's own images are not ours to take. Uses the earbuds silhouette.

jbl-flip-6.reason: jbl.com refuses automated requests on every regional host; Commons has Flip 3 and Flip 4 only. Uses the speaker silhouette.
